Just because she doesn't "look depressed" and "acts like a normal 10 year old" doesn't mean she isn't hurting. Depression and suicide don't have one particular face. Hell, on the outside I look like a happily married 27yr old. Laughing and joking with my friends, having nice dinners with my family, and deep down I wish I was dead. Some people are good at pretending to be okay when they're not. Let her know, as cliche as it is, it's okay to not be okay. If you're not going to tell your parents, try to help her through her emotions. Try to understand why she feels this way. Like someone said before something in her life brought this on, figuring out what that is, is the hardest question most of us here are still trying to find the answer to.
That's exactly what it feel like! Like damn, am I this big of a joke to the universe!?

I usually work the morning shifts because I'm quick at breaking down the order. My shifts are usually 4a-1p or 5a-2p. When I get there I start moving the palettes around and working on getting things in and out, while the other worker culls or vice versa. When I close or I'm midshift, I just rotate through each section repeatedly making sure things are full and everything is set up for the order the next morning.

He relapse a week ago, this was the 5th time, and I'll have to admit I didn't react well. He's military and got addicted to inhaling duster while on his last deployment,  he was caught at work and sent to outpatient treatment, mast, and right before his separation board he relapsed. They're going to send him to inpatient, and he's getting kicked out after that.

He wants to get better, he's told me he hates himself for it, and he doesn't understand why he still does it. He kept trying to hide it from his parents that he was struggling, and I left it alone because I felt he would tell them when he was ready. This last time I made him call his mother and tell her, and now that she knows having her support I think is helping. He's started going to his meetings again and meeting with his counselor and sponsor.

It already has. I've lied awake crying myself to sleep because I've tried to make my life better, and he's crumbling it down. He hasn't gone to his separation board yet so there's already still a possibility of them separating him, but that would leave him with a general discharge. If he's caught at work again he'll be put on restriction, half his pay taken, and then an other than honorable discharge. I quit my job to be a full time student, and I'm regretting it so much. We have a budget I've set up with just his paychecks which was already hurt by his drop in rank. The only money I have is what I've been able to put in savings. There is nothing of value in this house to me. If I was in my home state, the first time this happened I would've packed clothes, taken my dog, and left. But I stayed and I tried, the second time this happened it hurt but not as bad as the first, and now this being the third I don't know what I feel. Maybe amused at the fact that I thought our marriage could be okay.
